newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks seen tracking Wall St trends.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks seen tracking Wall St trends.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are likely to see more volatility in the early part of the week before caution sets in in advance of the release of key U.S. economic data, analysts said.
"We see potentially a flat market short term, going up and down with Wall Street whims," said Angus Steel, chief investment officer at Fortis Investments (Asia) Ltd.
The Hang Seng Index put on 104.58 points or 0.83 percent last week. It closed on 81.02 points, or 0.64 percent, lower at 12,645.76 on Friday, near the day's low of 12,643.28.
Friday turnover totalled HK$15.15 billion, the fourth heaviest on record, exchange figures showed.
Trading related to the expiry of the April Hang Seng Index futures contract on Tuesday could lift the index higher early in the week, brokers said.
The April contract closed 80 points lower at 12,645 on a par with the cash market.
But in the latter half of the week, the market was likely to move in line with trends on Wall Street and the U.S. bond market, analysts said.

"Hong Kong is clearly very highly correlated to the long end of the yield curve in the States," said Steel, adding that another interest rate rise in the United States and Hong Kong was possible in May.

On Friday, the benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond edged down 4/32 to close at 93-21/32 to yield 7.14 percent. Trading was relatively quiet, with the market awaiting several key economic reports due out this week, brokers said.

On Tuesday, the U.S. Employment Cost Index (ECI) for the first quarter of 1997, a report highlighted last year by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, will be released, followed by the first quarter Gross Domestic Product data report on Wednesday, and Labour Department data on Friday.
The reports are expected to confirm the robust growth trend of the U.S. economy, which could lead to further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, analysts said.
Technically, the market will remain locked in a trading range between 12,300 to 12,800, analysts said.
"We still need to see more basebuilding," said Chris Roberts, regional technical strategist at HSBC James Capel.

Considerable damage was done to some of the blue chips in the market's sell-off from its peak at 14,004.93, said Roberts, forecasting that the index could return to as low as 12,200 as part of the basebuilding programme.
Despite the negative factors, investors remain positive on the longer term outlook.

"We are pretty bullish. We think the property market will resume its uptrend in terms of residential prices in the second half and that will be coincident with rates coming down in the long end in the States," said Fortis' Steel.
For the time being, Fortis will remain overweight in Hong Kong and in red chips, Steel said.
Red chips have been the dominant theme of the market in recent weeks, are forecast to remain in the spotlight.
"Many of the China concept stocks are very expensive," said Charles Cheung. "I expect to see investors taking profit and subscribing to the new (red chip) issues."
It will also be another big week for red chip and H share earnings reports for 1996.
H share newcomer China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd will report its 1996 results on Monday as well as red chip Chinese software writer Founder (Hong Kong) Ltd.
